a.summary: The commit deleted two of the five accepted `PublicKey.verifySignature` NO_COVERAGE mutation sites but kept all five baseline rows per mutator, leaving four surplus accepted rows that permanently loosen the accounts mutation ratchet.
a.failure_scenario: Pre-commit the boolean-return NO_COVERAGE mutants for `PublicKey,verifySignature` sat at lines 106, 116, 159, 340 and 368; lines 159 and 368 were the return statements inside the two deprecated overloads this commit deletes, and old line 340 shifted to 325. So exactly three such mutants can exist post-commit, yet the file still carries five rows per mutator (lines 14-18 and 19-23). Because AGENTS.md makes baseline keys line-less (`class,method,mutator,STATUS`) and the gate compares counts, the ratchet now accepts 5 where reality is 3. Concretely: a later change that adds an uncovered `verifySignature` overload, or a test regression that uncovers two of the nine currently-covered boolean return sites (lines 46, 55, 66, 100, 130, 143, 148, 333, 342), raises the reported count from 3 to 5 - which exactly matches the accepted rows, so `pitestAccounts` still passes and the new coverage hole never surfaces.

b.summary: Four accepted `PublicKey.verifySignature` rows survive the deletion of their mutation sites and are tagged at a javadoc line (340) and past end-of-file (368), leaving two unclaimed acceptance slots per mutator that will silently absorb future NO_COVERAGE debt.
b.failure_scenario: Post-commit `PublicKey.java` has exactly three uncovered boolean-returning `verifySignature` sites reachable from `software.sava.core.accounts.*Test*`: lines 106 and 116 (the two unreachable private `Ed25519PublicKeyParameters` overloads) and line 325 (the 4-arg default, driven only from `core.tx` tests). The baseline holds five rows for `PublicKey,verifySignature,BooleanFalseReturnValsMutator,NO_COVERAGE` and five for the True twin. Add any new boolean `verifySignature` overload without an accounts-package test — plausible on an interface that already carries nine of them — and its two NO_COVERAGE mutants are absorbed by the two orphan rows: `pitestAccountsVerify` reports no new debt and stays green, which is exactly the "same-key swap is invisible" hole HARDENING_NOTES.md names, now pre-loaded with free slots.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
